correctness.rationale: Lücke–Poveda Theorem 1.3 produces a transitive set-sized ZFC model M satisfying that the exacting cardinals are unbounded in its own ordinals. The forward implication of Osinski Corollary 5.9 is a ZFC theorem (with logics and satisfaction definable in the stated sense), and holds internally in every such M. It gives one beth-fixed λ per logic, then a cardinal μ for each α<λ<ζ, with the inequalities and rank-type compactness exactly as stated. The theory-size restriction |T|=λ is Definition 5.3; Definition 3.2 actually defines size-unrestricted μ-chain compactness, while the rank-type definition is in the immediately preceding prose. That is a locator error, not a change in the proved hypothesis or conclusion. Neither an external class quantifier over arbitrary logics nor absoluteness of exactingness/compactness from M is needed. Replay by reading Lücke–Poveda v1 §1 Thm. 1.3 and Osinski v1 §2, §3 before Def. 3.2, §5 Def. 5.3 and Cor. 5.9 in the primary HTML. No lower bound or ambient-universe conclusion.
